en: O Śiva, Śaṅkara, who dwells within my heart along with Umā at the time of death—when there is excessive talk, harsh speech, the onset of death, and the torment of being struck by the hosts of Yama’s servants—remove me from the command of Yama; O Hara, take away my sin!

[O you] who are the supreme reproach for those whose merit is tainted by the pleasure arising from the objects of the wicked senses, and who have become deformed by the sins committed through seeking gratification [therein].

O supreme abode, protect me, protect me from all torment; O Śiva-Śaṅkara, Śiva-Śaṅkara, take away my [suffering], take away my sin! O Mṛḍa, protect me! Protect me with compassion along with Śivā from this desert land of the mind—a continuous succession of miseries, as beautiful as a baited hook called "objects of sense" smeared with ten thousand pieces of flesh—wherein I am intent. O Śiva-Śaṅkara, Śiva-Śaṅkara, take away my [suffering], take away my sin!
Protect my beloved wife, protect my daughter, protect my mother, and protect my father who has fixed his mind on the desolate desert lands.
O you who dwell with the woman born of sorrow, O wise one, O Śiva-Śaṅkara, Śiva-Śaṅkara, take away my suffering;
remove my sin! O destroyer of rebirth, O liberator from death, I have brought this [offering] to you, who are devoted to the worship of Śiva, as much as I am utterly emaciated by such [suffering].
O Śiva-Śaṅkara, O Śiva-Śaṅkara, O Hara, O Merciful One, remove my sin—[the sin of] making the flute produce weariness by [playing it] upon the trunks of elephants and the shells of tortoises!
While You, the Supreme Soul who abides in all existence, remain present, those whose eyes are wretched in their longing for wealth turn their minds away from Śiva;
they neglect their daily rites and fail to fast. O Śiva-Śaṅkara, O Śiva-Śaṅkara, O Hara, remove my sin!
"O parents! When indeed will this happen? O you who have joined my heart with the auspicious state of the two [Śiva and Śivā], go toward that wide station of the bounteous one through your own merit.

Thus, O Śiva, my heart has been seized by the desire for you; O Śiva-Śaṅkara, Śiva-Śaṅkara, remove it, remove my evil! (7) O ocean of the nectar of compassion, devoted to the protection of those who seek refuge, O Śiva-Bhava, whose dwelling is within the cycle of worldly existence, your feet are my refuge.
O Śiva, Śaṅkara, the supreme physician for the maladies of the world consisting of pure consciousness, who is praised by all—protect me! O Hara, remove my sin!

8 O Destroyer of Tripura, Lord of the gods, Leader of the Gaṇas, O Śiva, be my refuge! O you whose feet have the serpent of the ocean as their bracelet, O Bull-vehicled One, O Purifier of Poison, O Uplifter of the fallen, O Śiva, Śaṅkara, be my refuge! O Hara, remove my sin! 9
O moon-crested one, bestower of auspiciousness, you who lie upon Hari, beloved leader of the Daughter of the Mountain; O elephant-necked one, destroyer of the elephant-demon;
O destroyer of Kanaka’s throne and golden garments, refuge of all! O Śiva, Śaṅkara, Śiva, Śaṅkara, remove my sin, remove it!

(10) O conqueror of the senses, worshipped by the wise, whose feet are like stainless lotuses, destroyer of worldly existence, destroyer of fear; O you whose heart is marked by those who have taken refuge in you!
O Adorned with Serpents, O Nourisher of the Sage, O Destroyer of Madana, O Refuge, O Śivaśaṅkara—O Śivaśaṅkara, remove my sin! 11.
